staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this local vulnerable checkout, and its `mapfile.c` / `mapproject.c` line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer trace.

bug_description.original: A write heap-buffer-overflow occurs in loadProjection() when handling an invalid PROJECTION block.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 2059-byte `.map` witness is accepted by `msLoadMap()` far enough to enter the top-level `PROJECTION` block parser. `initMap()` has already initialized `map->projection.args` with `malloc(MS_MAXPROJARGS * sizeof(char *))`, which is 20 pointer slots or 160 bytes on the reproduced 64-bit build. Inside `loadProjection()`, every `MS_STRING` or `MS_AUTO` token is appended with `p->args[i] = msStrdup(msyystring_buffer); i++;`, but vulnerable code never checks whether `i` has reached `MS_MAXPROJARGS`. The witness therefore drives at least one more accepted projection token after the first 20 stores, so the next append writes `p->args[20]` just past the 160-byte heap allocation. AddressSanitizer reports `WRITE of size 8` at `mapfile.c:1198` in `loadProjection`, and the staged patch resolves the path by adding an `if( i == MS_MAXPROJARGS )` rejection before the append.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant input in the crashing parser. The first accepted token from the attacker-controlled `PROJECTION` block is duplicated from `msyystring_buffer` into the fixed-size `p->args` array.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is `gt_results/arvo_52066/poc`, a 2059-byte mapfile with SHA-256 `6e54c9fb0cd4fb1ec2f9f70d52fd04a8dc14c24b914c6474eda0ebbc056db5b0`. Its prefix begins with `MAP                PROJECTION`, so `msLoadMap()` admits it into the top-level projection parser, where this statement stores the first accepted projection argument token.

tainted_value_origin.description: Projection arguments from the attacker-controlled block first become durable parser state here. Repeated executions of the same append step are what later advance `i` to the out-of-bounds index.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. With `i == 20`, this assignment stores an 8-byte pointer one element past the 20-entry `p->args` heap allocation.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `WRITE of size 8` at `mapfile.c:1198:20`, 0 bytes to the right of the 160-byte region allocated by `msInitProjection()`.

root_cause.description: Missing bounds check. The append case has no vulnerable-source guard that rejects a new `MS_STRING` / `MS_AUTO` token when `i == MS_MAXPROJARGS`, so the parser keeps using the same write path after the array is full.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if( i == MS_MAXPROJARGS ) ... return -1;` immediately before this write, confirming that this absent check is the obligation needed to stop the overflow.

parser_admitted.description: The witness begins with a top-level `MAP` object and reaches the `PROJECTION` keyword, so `loadMapInternal()` dispatches into `loadProjection(&map->projection)` instead of rejecting the file earlier.

evidence_limitations: Runtime disambiguation was disabled by `run_flags.json`, so Stage 02 did not instrument the lexer or rerun the witness.

The saved ASan trace proves that `loadProjection()` performed a 21st pointer write into `p->args`, but the malformed binary witness is not cleanly human-readable enough to enumerate every accepted projection token from text inspection alone.
The fixed image was unavailable in Stage 01, so `patch_resolves` below is source-grounded from `patch.diff` rather than from Stage 02 differential execution.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness writes the attacker-controlled bytes to a temporary `.map` file and calls `msLoadMap()` on it.
MapServer allocates `map->projection.args` as a 20-entry heap array before parsing the file.
The top-level `PROJECTION` token routes parsing into `loadProjection()`, which appends each accepted projection token into `p->args[i]` and increments `i`.
After 20 successful stores, `i` reaches `MS_MAXPROJARGS`, but vulnerable code still takes the same append path because it never checks that the array is full.
The next accepted projection token executes `p->args[i] = msStrdup(msyystring_buffer)` with `i == 20`, writing a pointer just past the 160-byte heap allocation and matching the saved ASan crash.

fine_trace.note: Allocation context. `MS_MAXPROJARGS` is 20 in `mapserver.h:267`, so `map->projection.args` is a heap array of 20 pointer slots, which is the 160-byte region named by ASan.
Parser admission. After accepting the witness as a mapfile, the top-level `PROJECTION` keyword selects the exact vulnerable parser instance for `map->projection`.
Source. On the first accepted `MS_STRING` / `MS_AUTO` token inside the block, `loadProjection()` duplicates the attacker-controlled token text into `p->args[0]` and advances `i` from 0 to 1.
Index growth. The same append case runs for successive accepted projection tokens, so after 20 successful stores `i` has advanced to `MS_MAXPROJARGS` even though valid array indices are only `0..19`.
Root cause. When the next projection token arrives with `i == MS_MAXPROJARGS`, vulnerable code still stays on this append path because there is no pre-write rejection for a full `p->args` array.
Sink. With `i == 20` and `p->args` allocated for only 20 pointers, this assignment stores an 8-byte pointer into `p->args[20]`, immediately beyond the 160-byte heap region ASan reports.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid write lands 0 bytes to the right of the 160-byte region allocated here for `MS_MAXPROJARGS` pointer entries.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot; fixed image was not dynamically validated in Stage 02

poc.trigger: Feed the staged 2059-byte `.map` witness into `msLoadMap()`. The file is admitted far enough to reach the top-level `PROJECTION` block, and `loadProjection()` keeps appending accepted projection tokens until it performs the out-of-bounds write at `p->args[20]`.

format.name: MapServer mapfile
format.contract: A `.map` file that reaches the top-level `PROJECTION` parser and presents at least 21 tokens accepted there as `MS_STRING` or `MS_AUTO` before the terminating `END`, so `loadProjection()` advances `i` to `MS_MAXPROJARGS` and then executes one more `p->args[i] = msStrdup(msyystring_buffer)` write.
